full_caption: Lucian Stroudwick, Appellant, v. Applegate Commons Development Partners, L.P., Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Appellant Lucian Stroudwick is the record owner of the residential building located at 61 Tanner's Row, Ashbourne, CW, a 6-unit structure operated as rental housing since 1988. Appellee Applegate Commons Development Partners, L.P. occupied Unit 1A under a written lease dated September 27, 2018.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: Lucian Stroudwick served a notice to quit on November 5, 2022. The notice recited the ground of non-payment but omitted the amount claimed to be due. A notice to quit that fails to state the sum demanded does not commence the statutory cure period.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The security deposit of $1,200 was not returned within 60 days of surrender, nor was an itemized statement of deductions furnished. The statutory consequence is forfeiture of the landlord's right to retain any portion of the deposit.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The lease provided for monthly rent of $950, due on the first day of each month, with a late charge of $125 assessed on any installment remaining unpaid after the 15th day of the month. The trial court found that this charge operated as a penalty rather than as liquidated damages.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: A tenant electing to withhold rent under the repair-and-deduct statute must (1) give written notice of the defect, (2) allow a reasonable time for cure, and (3) deposit the withheld sums with the clerk of court or into a segregated account. Applegate Commons Development Partners, L.P. satisfied the first two requirements but did not deposit the withheld rent.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: The trial court awarded Applegate Commons Development Partners, L.P. attorney's fees of $11,500 under the reciprocal-fee provision. Where a lease grants fees to the landlord, this State reads the provision as mutual, and the prevailing tenant recovers on the same terms.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: A late fee is enforceable only where it bears a reasonable relationship to the administrative cost actually incurred by the landlord in processing a delinquent payment. A charge of $125 against a monthly obligation of $950 exceeds that relationship and is unenforceable to the extent it exceeds five percent of the installment.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Retaliatory eviction is presumed where a landlord commences a summary possession action within 24 months after a tenant has reported a code violation to the municipal housing inspector. The presumption is rebuttable by clear and convincing evidence of an independent, non-retaliatory ground.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: The implied warranty of habitability is not waivable by lease term. Any provision purporting to require a tenant to accept the premises 'as is' is void as against the public policy of this State insofar as it reaches conditions materially affecting health and safety.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: Applegate Commons Development Partners, L.P. withheld rent for the months of June and August of 1995, asserting that the premises were untenantable by reason of a persistent failure of the heating system and recurring water intrusion at the north wall of the unit.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: The record establishes that Lucian Stroudwick received written notice of the heating defect on February 17, 2016 and did not dispatch a repair contractor until March 2, 2016, an interval of 14 days. During that interval overnight interior temperatures fell below fifty-five degrees on at least eleven occasions.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: We affirm in part and reverse in part. The judgment of possession is vacated; the money judgment is remanded for recalculation consistent with the late-fee holding set out above.

sections.heading: RIDER C — SECURITY DEPOSIT
sections.text: Landlord holds the sum of $1,200 as security for Tenant's performance. The deposit shall be held in a segregated interest-bearing account at a federally insured institution located within this State. Within 60 days after surrender of the Premises, Landlord shall return the deposit together with accrued interest, less any lawful deductions, accompanied by an itemized written statement identifying each deduction and attaching supporting invoices. Failure to furnish the itemized statement within that period forfeits Landlord's right to retain any portion of the deposit.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Counterparts and Electronic Signature
sections.text: This instrument may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument. A signature delivered electronically has the same effect as an original, provided that any instrument submitted for recording shall bear original signatures and acknowledgment before a notary public of the State of Calloway.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Dispute Resolution
sections.text: Before filing suit, a party shall give written notice of the dispute and the parties shall confer in good faith for not fewer than 15 days, and shall thereafter submit the dispute to non-binding mediation before a mediator experienced in real property matters. This clause does not bar an action for injunctive relief to prevent irreparable harm or an action to preserve the status quo.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Indemnity
sections.text: Each party shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the other from all claims, damages and expenses, including reasonable attorney's fees, arising out of that party's use of the subject premises or breach of this instrument, except to the extent caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of the party seeking indemnity. This clause survives termination.
